ours: Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.
theirs: Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin--; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.

ours: LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.>> LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many [are] they that rise up against me.

ours: HEAR me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me when I was in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David.>> Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me [when I was] in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer.

ours: GIVE ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Nehiloth, A Psalm of David.>> Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.

ours: O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

ours: O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:
theirs: <<Shiggaion of David, which he sang unto the LORD, concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.>> O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me:

ours: O LORD our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD our Lord, how excellent [is] thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

ours: I WILL praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Muthlabben, A Psalm of David.>> I will praise [thee], O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.

ours: IN the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee as a bird to your mountain?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> In the LORD put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee [as] a bird to your mountain?

ours: HELP, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.>> Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; for the faithful fail from among the children of men.

ours: HOW long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?

ours: THE fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, [there is] none that doeth good.

ours: LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> LORD, who shall abide in thy tabernacle? who shall dwell in thy holy hill?

ours: PRESERVE me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.
theirs: <<Michtam of David.>> Preserve me, O God: for in thee do I put my trust.

ours: HEAR the right, O LORD, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, that goeth not out of feigned lips.
theirs: <<A Prayer of David.>> Hear the right, O LORD, attend unto my cry, give ear unto my prayer, [that goeth] not out of feigned lips.

ours: I WILL love thee, O LORD, my strength.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David, the servant of the LORD, who spake unto the LORD the words of this song in the day [that] the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul: And he said,>> I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.

ours: THE heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

ours: THE LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The LORD hear thee in the day of trouble; the name of the God of Jacob defend thee;

ours: THE king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> The king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!

ours: MY God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Aijeleth Shahar, A Psalm of David.>> My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? [why art thou so] far from helping me, [and from] the words of my roaring?

ours: THE LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The LORD [is] my shepherd; I shall not want.

ours: THE earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The earth [is] the LORD's, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

ours: UNTO thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.

ours: JUDGE me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; therefore I shall not slide.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD; [therefore] I shall not slide.

ours: THE LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> The LORD [is] my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD [is] the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

ours: UNTO thee will I cry, O LORD my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Unto thee will I cry, O LORD my rock; be not silent to me: lest, [if] thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

ours: GIVE unto the LORD, O ye mighty, give unto the LORD glory and strength.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> Give unto the LORD, O ye mighty, give unto the LORD glory and strength.

ours: I WILL extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.
theirs: <<A Psalm [and] Song [at] the dedication of the house of David.>> I will extol thee, O LORD; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.

ours: IN thee, O LORD, do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness.

ours: BLESSED is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David, Maschil.>> Blessed [is he whose] transgression [is] forgiven, [whose] sin [is] covered.

ours: I WILL bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David, when he changed his behaviour before Abimelech; who drove him away, and he departed.>> I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise [shall] continually [be] in my mouth.

ours: PLEAD my cause, O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Plead [my cause], O LORD, with them that strive with me: fight against them that fight against me.

ours: THE transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, that there is no fear of God before his eyes.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David the servant of the LORD.>> The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, [that there is] no fear of God before his eyes.

ours: FRET not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.

ours: O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, to bring to remembrance.>> O LORD, rebuke me not in thy wrath: neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.

ours: I SAID, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [even] to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David.>> I said, I will take heed to my ways, that I sin not with my tongue: I will keep my mouth with a bridle, while the wicked is before me.

ours: I WAITED patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry.

ours: BLESSED is he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Blessed [is] he that considereth the poor: the LORD will deliver him in time of trouble.

ours: AS the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Maschil, for the sons of Korah.>> As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O God.

ours: WE have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, Maschil.>> We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, [what] work thou didst in their days, in the times of old.

ours: MY heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, for the sons of Korah, Maschil, A Song of loves.>> My heart is inditing a good matter: I speak of the things which I have made touching the king: my tongue [is] the pen of a ready writer.

ours: GOD is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth.>> God [is] our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

ours: O CLAP your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph.

ours: GREAT is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.
theirs: <<A Song [and] Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> Great [is] the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, [in] the mountain of his holiness.

ours: HEAR this, all ye people; give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world:
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> Hear this, all [ye] people; give ear, all [ye] inhabitants of the world:

ours: THE mighty God, even the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> The mighty God, [even] the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.

ours: HAVE mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba.>> Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.

ours: WHY boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David, when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, and said unto him, David is come to the house of Ahimelech.>> Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God [endureth] continually.

ours: THE fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Mahalath, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David.>> The fool hath said in his heart, [There is] no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: [there is] none that doeth good.

ours: SAVE me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David, when the Ziphims came and said to Saul, Doth not David hide himself with us?>> Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me by thy strength.

ours: GIVE ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, Maschil, [A Psalm] of David.>> Give ear to my prayer, O God; and hide not thyself from my supplication.

ours: BE merciful unto me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Jonathelemrechokim, Michtam of David, when the Philistines took him in Gath.>> Be merciful unto me, O God: for man would swallow me up; he fighting daily oppresseth me.

ours: BE merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until these calamities be overpast.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David, when he fled from Saul in the cave.>> Be merciful unto me, O God, be merciful unto me: for my soul trusteth in thee: yea, in the shadow of thy wings will I make my refuge, until [these] calamities be overpast.

ours: DO ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David.>> Do ye indeed speak righteousness, O congregation? do ye judge uprightly, O ye sons of men?

ours: DELIVER me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, Michtam of David; when Saul sent, and they watched the house to kill him.>> Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.

ours: O GOD, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shushaneduth, Michtam of David, to teach; when he strove with Aramnaharaim and with Aramzobah, when Joab returned, and smote of Edom in the valley of salt twelve thousand.>> O God, thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us, thou hast been displeased; O turn thyself to us again.

ours: HEAR my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Neginah, [A Psalm] of David.>> Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.

ours: TRULY my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of David.>> Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him [cometh] my salvation.

ours: O GOD, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
theirs: <<A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.>> O God, thou [art] my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;

ours: HEAR my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

ours: PRAISE waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm [and] Song of David.>> Praise waiteth for thee, O God, in Sion: and unto thee shall the vow be performed.

ours: MAKE a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Song [or] Psalm.>> Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:

ours: GOD be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm [or] Song.>> God be merciful unto us, and bless us; [and] cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.

ours: LET God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm [or] Song of David.>> Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.

ours: SAVE me, O God; for the waters are come in unto my soul.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Shoshannim, [A Psalm] of David.>> Save me, O God; for the waters are come in unto [my] soul.

ours: MAKE haste, O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, [A Psalm] of David, to bring to remembrance.>> [Make haste], O God, to deliver me; make haste to help me, O LORD.

ours: GIVE the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] for Solomon.>> Give the king thy judgments, O God, and thy righteousness unto the king's son.

ours: TRULY God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> Truly God [is] good to Israel, [even] to such as are of a clean heart.

ours: O GOD, why hast thou cast us off for ever? why doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?
theirs: <<Maschil of Asaph.>> O God, why hast thou cast [us] off for ever? [why] doth thine anger smoke against the sheep of thy pasture?

ours: UNTO thee, O God, do we give thanks, unto thee do we give thanks: for that thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, Altaschith, A Psalm [or] Song of Asaph.>> Unto thee, O God, do we give thanks, [unto thee] do we give thanks: for [that] thy name is near thy wondrous works declare.

ours: IN Judah is God known: his name is great in Israel.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm [or] Song of Asaph.>> In Judah [is] God known: his name [is] great in Israel.

ours: I CRIED unto God with my voice, even unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun, A Psalm of Asaph.>> I cried unto God with my voice, [even] unto God with my voice; and he gave ear unto me.

ours: GIVE ear, O my people, to my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
theirs: <<Maschil of Asaph.>> Give ear, O my people, [to] my law: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

ours: O GOD, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.

ours: GIVE ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon ShoshannimEduth, A Psalm of Asaph.>> Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest [between] the cherubims, shine forth.

ours: SING aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, [A Psalm] of Asaph.>> Sing aloud unto God our strength: make a joyful noise unto the God of Jacob.

ours: GOD standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
theirs: <<A Psalm of Asaph.>> God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.

ours: KEEP not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm of Asaph.>> Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.

ours: HOW amiable are thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!
theirs: <<To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> How amiable [are] thy tabernacles, O LORD of hosts!

ours: LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm for the sons of Korah.>> LORD, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.

ours: BOW down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I am poor and needy.
theirs: <<A Prayer of David.>> Bow down thine ear, O LORD, hear me: for I [am] poor and needy.

ours: HIS foundation is in the holy mountains.
theirs: <<A Psalm [or] Song for the sons of Korah.>> His foundation [is] in the holy mountains.

ours: O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before thee:
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm for the sons of Korah, to the chief Musician upon Mahalath Leannoth, Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite.>> O LORD God of my salvation, I have cried day [and] night before thee:

ours: I WILL sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.
theirs: <<Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite.>> I will sing of the mercies of the LORD for ever: with my mouth will I make known thy faithfulness to all generations.

ours: LORD, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.
theirs: <<A Prayer of Moses the man of God.>> Lord, thou hast been our dwelling place in all generations.

ours: IT is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:
theirs: <<A Psalm [or] Song for the sabbath day.>> [It is a] good [thing] to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:

ours: O SING unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.
theirs: <<A Psalm.>> O sing unto the LORD a new song; for he hath done marvellous things: his right hand, and his holy arm, hath gotten him the victory.

ours: MAKE a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.
theirs: <<A Psalm of praise.>> Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.

ours: I WILL sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> I will sing of mercy and judgment: unto thee, O LORD, will I sing.

ours: HEAR my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.
theirs: <<A Prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed, and poureth out his complaint before the LORD.>> Hear my prayer, O LORD, and let my cry come unto thee.

ours: BLESS the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, [bless] his holy name.

ours: O GOD, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.
theirs: <<A Song [or] Psalm of David.>> O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory.

ours: HOLD not thy peace, O God of my praise;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Hold not thy peace, O God of my praise;

ours: THE LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.

ours: BLESSED are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.
theirs: ALEPH. Blessed [are] the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.

ours: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
theirs: BETH. Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed [thereto] according to thy word.

ours: Deal bountifully with thy servant, that I may live, and keep thy word.
theirs: GIMEL. Deal bountifully with thy servant, [that] I may live, and keep thy word.

ours: My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.
theirs: DALETH. My soul cleaveth unto the dust: quicken thou me according to thy word.

ours: Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it unto the end.
theirs: HE. Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes; and I shall keep it [unto] the end.

ours: Let thy mercies come also unto me, O LORD, even thy salvation, according to thy word.
theirs: VAU. Let thy mercies come also unto me, O LORD, [even] thy salvation, according to thy word.

ours: Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.
theirs: ZAIN. Remember the word unto thy servant, upon which thou hast caused me to hope.

ours: Thou art my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words.
theirs: CHETH. [Thou art] my portion, O LORD: I have said that I would keep thy words.

ours: Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD, according unto thy word.
theirs: TETH. Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD, according unto thy word.

ours: Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.
theirs: JOD. Thy hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, that I may learn thy commandments.

ours: My soul fainteth for thy salvation: but I hope in thy word.
theirs: CAPH. My soul fainteth for thy salvation: [but] I hope in thy word.

ours: For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.
theirs: LAMED. For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.

ours: O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.
theirs: MEM. O how love I thy law! it [is] my meditation all the day.

ours: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
theirs: NUN. Thy word [is] a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

ours: I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.
theirs: SAMECH. I hate [vain] thoughts: but thy law do I love.

ours: I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.
theirs: AIN. I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.

ours: Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.
theirs: PE. Thy testimonies [are] wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.

ours: Righteous art thou, O LORD, and upright are thy judgments.
theirs: TZADDI. Righteous [art] thou, O LORD, and upright [are] thy judgments.

ours: I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes.
theirs: KOPH. I cried with [my] whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes.

ours: Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.
theirs: RESH. Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.

ours: Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.
theirs: SCHIN. Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.

ours: Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word.
theirs: TAU. Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word.

ours: IN my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> In my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.

ours: I WILL lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

ours: I WAS glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the LORD.

ours: UNTO thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Unto thee lift I up mine eyes, O thou that dwellest in the heavens.

ours: IF it had not been the LORD who was on our side, now may Israel say;
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> If [it had] not [been] the LORD who was on our side, now may Israel say;

ours: THEY that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> They that trust in the LORD [shall be] as mount Zion, [which] cannot be removed, [but] abideth for ever.

ours: WHEN the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.

ours: EXCEPT the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees for Solomon.>> Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh [but] in vain.

ours: BLESSED is every one that feareth the LORD; that walketh in his ways.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Blessed [is] every one that feareth the LORD; that walketh in his ways.

ours: MANY a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:

ours: OUT of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD.

ours: LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> LORD, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty: neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me.

ours: LORD, remember David, and all his afflictions:
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> LORD, remember David, [and] all his afflictions:

ours: BEHOLD, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
theirs: <<A Song of degrees of David.>> Behold, how good and how pleasant [it is] for brethren to dwell together in unity!

ours: BEHOLD, bless ye the LORD, all ye servants of the LORD, which by night stand in the house of the LORD.
theirs: <<A Song of degrees.>> Behold, bless ye the LORD, all [ye] servants of the LORD, which by night stand in the house of the LORD.

ours: I WILL praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.

ours: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known [me].

ours: DELIVER me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;
theirs: <<To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David.>> Deliver me, O LORD, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man;

ours: LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> LORD, I cry unto thee: make haste unto me; give ear unto my voice, when I cry unto thee.

ours: I CRIED unto the LORD with my voice; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication.
theirs: <<Maschil of David; A Prayer when he was in the cave.>> I cried unto the LORD with my voice; with my voice unto the LORD did I make my supplication.

ours: HEAR my prayer, O LORD, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, and in thy righteousness.
theirs: <<A Psalm of David.>> Hear my prayer, O LORD, give ear to my supplications: in thy faithfulness answer me, [and] in thy righteousness.

ours: BLESSED be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight:
theirs: <<[A Psalm] of David.>> Blessed [be] the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, [and] my fingers to fight:

ours: I WILL extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.
theirs: <<David's [Psalm] of praise.>> I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever.

ours: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
theirs: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse. <<THE END OF THE PROPHETS.>>

ours: NOW when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judæa in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
theirs: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,

ours: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judæa: for thus it is written by the prophet,
theirs: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,

ours: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judæa in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:
theirs: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of God in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:

ours: IN those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judæa,
theirs: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea,

ours: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judæa, and all the region round about Jordan,
theirs: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan,

ours: And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and from Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judæa, and from beyond Jordan.
theirs: And there followed him great multitudes of people from Galilee, and [from] Decapolis, and [from] Jerusalem, and [from] Judaea, and [from] beyond Jordan.

ours: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphæus, and Lebbæus, whose surname was Thaddæus;
theirs: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James [the son] of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;

ours: When Jesus came into the coasts of Cæsarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
theirs: When Jesus came into the coasts of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?

ours: AND it came to pass, that when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judæa beyond Jordan;
theirs: And it came to pass, [that] when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee, and came into the coasts of Judaea beyond Jordan;

ours: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cæsar, or not?
theirs: Tell us therefore, What thinkest thou? Is it lawful to give tribute unto Caesar, or not?

ours: They say unto him, Cæsars. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsars; and unto God the things that are Gods.
theirs: They say unto him, Caesar's. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.

ours: Then let them which be in Judæa flee into the mountains:
theirs: Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains:

ours: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathæa, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus disciple:
theirs: When the even was come, there came a rich man of Arimathaea, named Joseph, who also himself was Jesus' disciple:

ours: And there went out unto him all the land of Judæa, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.
theirs: And there went out unto him all the land of Judaea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.

ours: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
theirs: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the [son] of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

ours: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judæa,
theirs: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,

ours: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumæa, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.
theirs: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and [from] beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.

ours: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphæus, and Thaddæus, and Simon the Canaanite,
theirs: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,

ours: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cæsarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
theirs: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

ours: AND he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judæa by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.
theirs: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the coasts of Judaea by the farther side of Jordan: and the people resort unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.

ours: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimæus, the son of Timæus, sat by the highway side begging.
theirs: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, sat by the highway side begging.

ours: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Cæsar, or not?
theirs: And when they were come, they say unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not?

ours: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Cæsars.
theirs: And they brought [it]. And he saith unto them, Whose [is] this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Caesar's.

ours: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Cæsar the things that are Cæsars, and to God the things that are Gods. And they marvelled at him.
theirs: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled at him.

ours: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand,) then let them that be in Judæa flee to the mountains:
theirs: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand,) then let them that be in Judaea flee to the mountains:

ours: And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilæan, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
theirs: And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art [one] of them: for thou art a Galilaean, and thy speech agreeth [thereto].

ours: And the soldiers led him away into the hall, called Prætorium; and they call together the whole band.
theirs: And the soldiers led him away into the hall, called Praetorium; and they call together the whole band.

ours: Joseph of Arimathæa, an honourable counseller, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.
theirs: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counseller, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

ours: THERE was in the days of Herod, the king of Judæa, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
theirs: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron, and her name [was] Elisabeth.

ours: And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judæa.
theirs: And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judaea.

ours: AND it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Cæsar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.
theirs: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.

ours: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judæa, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)
theirs: And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)

ours: NOW in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Cæsar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judæa, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituræa and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene,
theirs: Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias the tetrarch of Abilene,

ours: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judæa, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
theirs: And it came to pass on a certain day, as he was teaching, that there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting by, which were come out of every town of Galilee, and Judaea, and Jerusalem: and the power of the Lord was [present] to heal them.

ours: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
theirs: Matthew and Thomas, James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,

ours: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judæa and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;
theirs: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judaea and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;

ours: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judæa, and throughout all the region round about.
theirs: And this rumour of him went forth throughout all Judaea, and throughout all the region round about.

ours: THERE were present at that season some that told him of the Galilæans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
theirs: There were present at that season some that told him of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.

ours: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilæans were sinners above all the Galilæans, because they suffered such things?
theirs: And Jesus answering said unto them, Suppose ye that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?

ours: And, behold, there was a man named Zacchæus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
theirs: And, behold, [there was] a man named Zacchaeus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.

ours: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
theirs: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.

ours: And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
theirs: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore [him] fourfold.

ours: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Cæsar, or no?
theirs: Is it lawful for us to give tribute unto Caesar, or no?

ours: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Cæsars.
theirs: Shew me a penny. Whose image and superscription hath it? They answered and said, Caesar's.

ours: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which be Cæsars, and unto God the things which be Gods.
theirs: And he said unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which be Caesar's, and unto God the things which be God's.

ours: Then let them which are in Judæa flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.
theirs: Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto.

ours: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilæan.
theirs: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this [fellow] also was with him: for he is a Galilaean.

ours: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this fellow perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Cæsar, saying that he himself is Christ a King.
theirs: And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this [fellow] perverting the nation, and forbidding to give tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ a King.

ours: When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilæan.
theirs: When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.

ours: (The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them;) he was of Arimathæa, a city of the Jews: who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.
theirs: (The same had not consented to the counsel and deed of them;) [he was] of Arimathaea, a city of the Jews: who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.

ours: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judæa; and there he tarried with them, and baptized.
theirs: After these things came Jesus and his disciples into the land of Judaea; and there he tarried with them, and baptized.

ours: And John also was baptizing in Ænon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.
theirs: And John also was baptizing in AEnon near to Salim, because there was much water there: and they came, and were baptized.

ours: He left Judæa, and departed again into Galilee.
theirs: He left Judaea, and departed again into Galilee.

ours: Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galilæans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.
theirs: Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galilaeans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.

ours: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judæa into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death.
theirs: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death.

ours: This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judæa into Galilee.
theirs: This [is] again the second miracle [that] Jesus did, when he was come out of Judaea into Galilee.

ours: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judæa, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.
theirs: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judaea, that thy disciples also may see the works that thou doest.

ours: Then after that saith he to his disciples, Let us go into Judæa again.
theirs: Then after that saith he to [his] disciples, Let us go into Judaea again.

ours: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cæsars friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Cæsar.
theirs: And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Caesar's friend: whosoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.

ours: But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cæsar.
theirs: But they cried out, Away with [him], away with [him], crucify him. Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.

ours: And after this Joseph of Arimathæa, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.
theirs: And after this Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave [him] leave. He came therefore, and took the body of Jesus.

ours: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judæa, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
theirs: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

ours: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
theirs: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James [the son] of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas [the brother] of James.

ours: And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galilæans?
theirs: And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying one to another, Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans?

ours: Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judæa, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia,
theirs: Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judaea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia,

ours: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:
theirs: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice, and said unto them, Ye men of Judaea, and all [ye] that dwell at Jerusalem, be this known unto you, and hearken to my words:

ours: Then came he out of the land of the Chaldæans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell.
theirs: Then came he out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and dwelt in Charran: and from thence, when his father was dead, he removed him into this land, wherein ye now dwell.

ours: AND Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judæa and Samaria, except the apostles.
theirs: And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles.

ours: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached in all the cities, till he came to Cæsarea.
theirs: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached in all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.

ours: Which when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Cæsarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.
theirs: [Which] when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.

ours: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judæa and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.
theirs: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.

ours: And there he found a certain man named Æneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.
theirs: And there he found a certain man named AEneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.

ours: And Peter said unto him, Æneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.
theirs: And Peter said unto him, AEneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.

ours: THERE was a certain man in Cæsarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,
theirs: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian [band],

ours: And the morrow after they entered into Cæsarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.
theirs: And the morrow after they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius waited for them, and had called together his kinsmen and near friends.

ours: That word, I say, ye know, which was published throughout all Judæa, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;
theirs: That word, [I say], ye know, which was published throughout all Judaea, and began from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

ours: AND the apostles and brethren that were in Judæa heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
theirs: And the apostles and brethren that were in Judaea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.

ours: And, behold, immediately there were three men already come unto the house where I was, sent from Cæsarea unto me.
theirs: And, behold, immediately there were three men already come unto the house where I was, sent from Caesarea unto me.

ours: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Cæsar.
theirs: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar.

ours: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judæa:
theirs: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judaea:

ours: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judæa to Cæsarea, and there abode.
theirs: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that [they] should be put to death. And he went down from Judaea to Caesarea, and [there] abode.

ours: AND certain men which came down from Judæa taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.
theirs: And certain men which came down from Judaea taught the brethren, [and said], Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

ours: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cæsar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
theirs: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, [one] Jesus.

ours: And when he had landed at Cæsarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
theirs: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.

ours: And the next day we that were of Pauls company departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
theirs: And the next [day] we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was [one] of the seven; and abode with him.

ours: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.
theirs: And as we tarried [there] many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.

ours: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cæsarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
theirs: There went with us also [certain] of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.

ours: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
theirs: And he called unto [him] two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;

ours: Who, when they came to Cæsarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
theirs: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

ours: NOW when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cæsarea to Jerusalem.
theirs: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

ours: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cæsarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
theirs: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly [thither].

ours: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cæsarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
theirs: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.

ours: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cæsar, have I offended any thing at all.
theirs: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.

ours: Then said Paul, I stand at Cæsars judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
theirs: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.

ours: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
theirs: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.

ours: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cæsar? unto Cæsar shalt thou go.
theirs: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.

ours: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cæsarea to salute Festus.
theirs: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.

ours: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cæsar.
theirs: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.

ours: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
theirs: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and [then] to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.

ours: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
theirs: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.

ours: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cæsar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
theirs: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.

ours: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
theirs: But when the Jews spake against [it], I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.

ours: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judæa concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
theirs: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.

ours: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judæa; and that my service which I have for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;
theirs: That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judaea; and that my service which [I have] for Jerusalem may be accepted of the saints;

ours: Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epænetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.
theirs: Likewise [greet] the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.

ours: To God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
theirs: To God only wise, [be] glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen. <<[Written to the Romans from Corinthus, [and sent] by Phebe servant of the church at Cenchrea.]>>

ours: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
theirs: My love [be] with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi by Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, and Timotheus.]>>

ours: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judæa.
theirs: And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.

ours: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Corinthians was written from Philippi, [a city] of Macedonia, by Titus and Lucas.]>>

ours: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judæa which were in Christ:
theirs: And was unknown by face unto the churches of Judaea which were in Christ:

ours: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
theirs: Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen. <<[Unto the Galatians written from Rome.]>>

ours: Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen.
theirs: Grace [be] with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in sincerity. Amen. <<[Written from Rome unto the Ephesians by Tychicus.]>>

ours: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Cæsars household.
theirs: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Caesar's household.

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<[It was written to the Philippians from Rome by Epaphroditus.]>>

ours: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
theirs: The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace [be] with you. Amen. <<[Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.]>>

ours: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judæa are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews:
theirs: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judaea are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they [have] of the Jews:

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you. Amen. <<[The first [epistle] unto the Thessalonians was written from Athens.]>>

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] to the Thessalonians was written from Athens.]>>

ours: Of whom is Hymenæus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
theirs: Of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

ours: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with thee. Amen.
theirs: Which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace [be] with thee. Amen. <<[The first to Timothy was written from Laodicea, which is the chiefest city of Phrygia Pacatiana.]>>

ours: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenæus and Philetus;
theirs: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;

ours: The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.
theirs: The Lord Jesus Christ [be] with thy spirit. Grace [be] with you. Amen. <<[The second [epistle] unto Timotheus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Ephesians, was written from Rome, when Paul was brought before Nero the second time.]>>

ours: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.
theirs: All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace [be] with you all. Amen. <<[It was written to Titus, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Cretians, from Nicopolis of Macedonia.]>>

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen. <<[Written from Rome to Philemon, by Onesimus a servant.]>>

ours: Grace be with you all. Amen.
theirs: Grace [be] with you all. Amen. <<[Written to the Hebrews from Italy by Timothy.]>>

ours: Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: but he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also.
theirs: Whosoever denieth the Son, the same hath not the Father: [(but) he that acknowledgeth the Son hath the Father also].

ours: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
theirs: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you all. Amen. <<THE END.>>
